calls.head: Dallas hunts better looks than Nashville
calls.body: On shot quality, Dallas sits 3rd of 32, at the point-blank end of the scale. Nashville is 28th, at the perimeter end.
calls.call: Dallas’s shots are more dangerous on average than Nashville’s.

calls.happened: On how dangerous the average unblocked shot was, Dallas had 1 goal per 23.4 shots and Nashville 1 goal per 21.1 shots. Coming in, Dallas was at 1 goal per 14.6 shots and Nashville at 1 goal per 16.8 shots.

calls.head: Dallas’s power play outclasses Nashville’s
calls.body: On power play, Dallas sits 3rd of 32, at the lethal end of the scale. Nashville is 25th, at the harmless end.
calls.call: Dallas’s power play creates more per 60 than Nashville’s.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On power-play expected goals per 60, Dallas had 13.9 per 60 and Nashville 3.8 per 60. Coming in, Dallas was at 8.6 per 60 and Nashville at 7.3 per 60.

NSH.head: We had this close to even (51% for Nashville), and Nashville came through.

DAL.head: We had this close to even (49% for Dallas), and it went Nashville’s way.

surprises.head: Dallas was kept to the outside
surprises.body: Dallas needed 23.4 unblocked shots per expected goal at 5-on-5, against its usual 14.6 and a league average of 15.8. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 80 games.
